Bounty Hunter.description:
Whether in pursuit of escaped prisoners, runaway debtors, or prodigal heirs, bounty hunters ruthlessly chase their prey for as long as the money's good. While many targets are wanted "dead or alive," or plain and simply "dead," the hunter below specializes in bringing targets back alive using their magbolas and shock weapons.

Mercenaries

So long as the almighty credit can buy power, safety, and comfort, it can also be used to buy violence from the desperate, irrational, and unsentimental. Absalom Station is home to countless mercenary companies and freelance soldiers-for-hire, all eagerly offering their services to the highest bidder.

Some mercs have a moral code or sense of honor that limits what contracts they accept, and Absalom law strictly limits what jobs a paramilitary company can hand out to its members. Of course, this doesn't stop a festering underbelly of wetwork and worse from blooming in the darker reaches of the station, if one knows where to look.

Mercenaries aren't always operatives or soldiers. Sometimes they're cunning spellcasters, powerful solarians, or treacherous envoys. Bounty hunters are one of the most common class of merc hanging around the station. The bounty hunter below is an example of an elite foe tracking down dangerous outlaws, but the statistics for gangsters can stand in for lower-level mercenaries.

DSKLDbuJc2B4i9DG.name: Not So Fast

A creature that fails this save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed} for 1 round (2 rounds on a critical failure). They can't use Gauntlet Flamethrower again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Gauntlet Flamethrower]]{1d4 rounds}.
dBUYgBiKNoptvmHG.name: Gauntlet Flamethrower

Credshark.description:
Credsharks operate on the higher end of the food chain.

Gangsters

Criminal guilds, crime families, protection rackets, and loan sharks are just a few of the many types of gangs in Absalom Station. Gangs are highly localized, predatory, and extremely territorial. Members join for different reasons, but most find that once they're in a gang, there's no easy way out.

Gangsters always have hustles, criminal industries they use to make money, but most also operate protection rackets as a matter of course. Business owners within a gang's territory (or worse, in the overlapping territories of more than one gang) can expect to pay regularly or risk severe consequences.

5AKbY6oL40YCDQmG.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The credshark commands one of their allies to attack a creature. The ally can use a reaction to Strike the designated creature. If the ally hits, the target must also succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.
5AKbY6oL40YCDQmG.name: Make an Example

8S2JV16ASWWmAh1T.description: These ubiquitous handheld computers incorporate a comm unit, microphone, speaker, camera, infosphere browser, and data storage. They can store thousands of hours of recordings, play games, and perform simple computing functions, such as time tracking and notifications, word processing, calculations, data processing, streaming media, and broadcasting emergency alerts from local governments. In most societies, commercial datapads are relatively flimsy, designed to rapidly wear out or fall behind on the latest features and updates to encourage the consumer to replace it with a newer model. In contrast, higher-end datapads are made to last and often include a sturdier chassis and extra functions.
8S2JV16ASWWmAh1T.name: Datapad (Loaded with financial and bookkeeping apps)

Credshark.name: Credshark

Cryo Mist.description: Hidden nozzles in the ceiling release hyper-cold air, potentially freezing intruders in place.
Cryo Mist.hazardDisable: @Check[computers|dc:27] (master) to increase the air's temperature to safe levels, or @Check[thievery|dc:27] (master) to deactivate the nozzles

Deadly Vidgame.description: A hyperrealistic vidgame pulls players into a virtual world, transforming them into pixelated avatars and pitting them against deadly challenges.
Deadly Vidgame.hazardDisable: @Check[computers|dc:22] (trained) to reprogram the game, or @Check[thievery|dc:22] (trained) to exploit a glitch, or @Check[vidgame-lore|dc:17] (trained) to beat the game; four total successes are required to disable the trap
Deadly Vidgame.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The trap presents the game's players with deadly challenges as 1 action. Each creature inside the game takes @Damage[(2d8+5)[slashing]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). A creature can attempt a Vidgame Lore check in place of their saving throw, if desired.
Deadly Vidgame.name: Deadly Vidgame

Devastating Collision.description: A phantom hover truck collides with creatures, replaying an accident from the past in gory detail.

Devastating Collision.name: Devastating Collision

Distracting Holo Ad.hazardDisable: @Check[computers|dc:17] (trained) to deactivate the ad, or @Check[crafting|dc:20] (trained) or Thievery (trained) to disable the projector
Distracting Holo Ad.hazardReset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.
Distracting Holo Ad.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The hazard plays a new ad each round, forcing all creatures that can sense it to attempt a new save.
Distracting Holo Ad.name: Distracting Holo Ad

ICJNXNcPqawzZ5Di.description: This vehicle protects its users from the dangers of space, including the benefits of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.FLODmOj4yK7eJn0a]{Basic Environmental Protection} and a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.0kD0MZgiK0SYS6e6]{Commercial Filtered Rebreather}.
ICJNXNcPqawzZ5Di.name: Space Vehicle

One round before impact, antigrav rotors, parachutes, and retrorockets slow the descent to 60 feet per round, allowing for a safe landing (even if uncontrolled).
Sj8NcT54mE0h1du1.name: Controlled Plummet

otJCE9pNtnC9pjtp.description: The pilot and passengers of a drop pod are completely enclosed and don't have line of sight or line of effect with any creatures or objects outside the vehicle.

Assassins for hire tend to be cold pragmatists who might do anything for the right price, but many have their own strange philosophies or belong to obscure cults and religious sects. Graviton Assassin.name: Graviton Assassin

Haywire Robotic Arm.name: Haywire Robotic Arm

0APyn1dCXX5CcX6K.description: The hoverboard can be carried as an item with 1 Bulk.
0APyn1dCXX5CcX6K.name: Portable

G4rVP7ST3gSmfmeq.description: A hoverboard maintains an altitude of 6 inches above other surfaces, such as the ground or water. If driven off a high surface, the hoverboard loses 20 feet of altitude per round, landing without harm to the hoverboard or its pilot.

Jolting Console.description: A shock grid built into a computer console or door panel releases a powerful electric charge.

Jolting Console.name: Jolting Console

Laser Turret.description: A concealed turret pops up and fires a laser when intruders enter a secure area.

Laser Web.name: Laser Web

Starstone Guardian.description:
The magicircuitry patterns etched on the surface of each Starstone guardian's body are unique. They tell the story of each guardian's creation ritual. Though incredibly ancient, the magic that sustains the Starstone guardians refreshes and restores them over time, making Starstone guardians effectively immortal. These constructs often become uncomfortable if addressed as if they're distinct individuals. If asked for a designation, each insists they are to be referred to simply as "Guardian."

More powerful iterations of the guardians were created to protect the reactor's network of facilities, called the prime virtues by the engineers and historians who study them. With few exceptions, the prime virtues are rarely encountered by ordinary people. All have unique features and personalities that make such experiences unforgettable, and sometimes dangerous. The characteristics and capabilities of the prime virtues aren't well understood for this reason.

Starstone guardians are peaceful when they aren't deployed to protect the reactor network keeping the entire space station spinning, but their defenses aren't infallible. Corrupted or controlled Starstone guardians are more likely to attack.

STARSTONE CONSTRUCTS

Starstone constructs are ancient magitech constructs that serve to protect and maintain the Starstone reactor, the station's power source fueled by the legendary Starstone. They are reticent and standoffish creatures whose sole area of concern is the reactor and its continued functionality. Starstone constructs are vigilant and pious, performing their duties with unmistakable reverence. They are almost never seen outside of the Spike, and only rarely outside the chambers around the Starstone reactor. They attempt to complete whatever tasks take them away from their primary focus quickly and efficiently.

Starstone constructs are tall, broad-shouldered robotic humanoids of gleaming platinum with slender limbs made of a translucent blue crystal. Their faces are mask-like and nearly featureless but for three circular eye holes containing luminous spheres that blink, widen, narrow, and otherwise move like a biological creature's eyes. Each Starstone construct has a pattern of intricate magicircuitry etched into their crystalline limbs and down the sides of their metallic torso.

Starstone constructs have humanlike forms but don't follow most humanoid customs and habits, except for a custom of adorning themselves with cloth drapery, similar to how a humanoid would wear clothing. Starstone stoles are embroidered with spelled thread and are believed to contain immense magical energy.

These sleek but sturdy shields are designed to protect most of the wielder's body when raised while allowing them to march in tight tactical formations. Sometimes they're transparent to allow inexperienced wielders to see the other side while the shield is raised, but most experienced warriors have no problem seeing around these shields, and the transparent material quickly becomes too scuffed to see through after a few hits.

Starstone sentries maintain the Starstone reactor and guard its approaches against intruders. Each Starstone sentry was created from a Starstone guardian and bears a magicircuitry pattern of that guardian, although the sentry's circuitry is neither an exact duplicate nor a perfect reflection. It's not clear what prompts Starstone guardians to create these sentries, or even what the process for creating them entails, but more Starstone sentries appear, glowing and new, before times of great danger to the Starstone or upheaval on Absalom Station.

Slightly smaller and more fragile than their guardian progenitors, Starstone sentries are nevertheless just as diligent about protecting the Starstone-powered reactor at the heart of Absalom Station. Starstone sentries act and speak in unnerving symmetry, especially when they are close together. Despite having a superficial appearance that matches one specific guardian more than any others, every Starstone sentry unfailingly follows directions of any guardian.

String-of-Bombs.description:
The string-of-bombs is a beautiful yet explosive succulent that can be found as a dangerous passenger aboard many starships in the Pact Worlds. Native to the jungles of Castrovel, the string-of-bombs' explosive name comes from the softly glowing orange pods that dangle from their vines. These pods were developed as a defense mechanism against Castrovel's massive predators when thorns and vines proved insufficient deterrents.

As the plant's explosive pods don't develop until full maturity, the string-of-bombs resembles other harmless succulents (including the closely related and harmless string-of-suns) and might be overlooked as low-maintenance ship greenery. Many gardeners remain unaware of the hazard they're cultivating until it literally blows up in their face.

Infestations

Invasive creatures plague Absalom Station and resist the most dedicated efforts to eliminate them. Whether lurking in the Ghost Levels or stowing away on starships, tenacious infestations are a constant problem in such a large and cosmopolitan station.

Terminite Hunter.description:
When stories of terminites first spread, they were viewed as eerie, furtive scavengers. When thrill-seekers began hunting the creatures for sport or study, a new type of terminite appeared almost overnight: the terminite hunter. Hunters are far more bloodthirsty than the smaller worker components of a terminite colony. Instead of harvesting motes from objects and terrain, hunters are strong enough to rip chunks of reality from living creatures.

Infestations

Invasive creatures plague Absalom Station and resist the most dedicated efforts to eliminate them. Whether lurking in the Ghost Levels or stowing away on starships, tenacious infestations are a constant problem in such a large and cosmopolitan station.

If the terminite doesn't have a mote (see below), it gains a mote of the target's essence that vanishes after 24 hours. While the terminite has this mote, it knows the distance and direction to the target.

Terminite queens control their colonies and most other "lesser" creatures like puppets. When it's time to multiply, the queen produces clones of the components by sacrificing parts of her body. The motes collected by subordinate terminites in turn nourish the queen. When threatened, queens absorb occult energies from the motes, which they can shape into illusory scenes and blasts of reality-rending power.

Wherever a queen goes, a colony is sure to follow.

Terminite Worker.description:
Among the urban legends and scary stories traded by Absalom's urban explorers, few are as ubiquitous as tales of "void bugs." Exact descriptions vary, and even camera footage is inconsistent, but stories agree on spindly appendages reaching out from impossible spaces, perfectly tessellated pieces missing from machines, and multi-legged shadows flowing like eerie, gangly waves down corridors just out of view. Some Ghost Couriers have made a point of learning more about these creatures, which they've dubbed terminites.

Terminites have proved hard to study because they live in a nest built in folds of strange space behind the Universe but accessed through the Ghost Levels. Some Ghost Couriers liken terminites to certain eusocial insects; after all, these anomalies infest the walls of reality like ordinary pests in mundane structures. Truthfully, however, a naturalistic description of these creatures undersells them. Terminites are enthralled reflections of their queen: a cryptic overmind permanently ensconced in the nest she's built behind reality in the Ghost Levels. Few explorers have accessed this nest-reality, and none so far have returned, though disjointed recordings or logs of their travels survive. The queen seems omnipresent in the nest; within, her brood take on a nightmarish infinity of specialized forms. Fortunately, the queen seems content to bide her time, at least for now.

The most commonly encountered terminites are the workers, fragments of the queen's will formed as scouts and salvagers. Terminite workers focus on breaking down physical objects, usually ones with obscure occult resonance, and returning them to the nest for their queen's inscrutable purposes.

Infestations

Invasive creatures plague Absalom Station and resist the most dedicated efforts to eliminate them. Whether lurking in the Ghost Levels or stowing away on starships, tenacious infestations are a constant problem in such a large and cosmopolitan station.

Effect The terminite can spend 1 minute to dig a tunnel in reality to or from its extradimensional nest. Non-terminites see this "tunnel" as a shimmering sphere of color that occupies a 10-foot sphere. Creatures in the sphere are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and all creatures outside the sphere are concealed from creatures within it. Terminites can pass through the sphere to the nest; for other creatures, the sphere is difficult terrain but doesn't lead anywhere. The tunnel closes after 1 minute. A reality tunnel can be destroyed by dispel magic automatically or by manipulating it with an Interact action and a successful @Check[occultism|dc:16] check.

Thaumacyte.description:
In the gas-rich atmosphere of Liavara , magically enlarged aeroplankton make up the bottom of the planet's food chain. Beginning as simple filter feeders, many species of plankton were transformed by vibrations from the Dreamers' wordless songs. The thaumacyte is one such organism, having evolved in areas rich with thaumogen gas and growing much larger than typical microorganisms due to occult interference.

Thaumacytes look like shifting sacs containing iridescent fluid and colorful organelles. A magically reinforced spell membrane allows these floating amoeboids to survive in a variety of environments. After stowing away on unregulated thaumogen mining vessels, some of these unicellular oddities have spread throughout the Pact Worlds. As they feel a particular pull toward powerful magic like the Starstone, many thaumacytes lurk in Absalom Station.

Most thaumacytes grow to be about 3 feet wide and are usually translucent with a hint of warmer hues, a coloration useful for hiding in Liavara's atmosphere but making them strange and obvious in most of Absalom Station.

Tough.description:
Toughs are low-ranking gang members who act as lookouts, messengers, or muscle for more powerful criminals. Where there's one tough, more are surely nearby.

Gangsters

Criminal guilds, crime families, protection rackets, and loan sharks are just a few of the many types of gangs in Absalom Station. Gangs are highly localized, predatory, and extremely territorial. Members join for different reasons, but most find that once they're in a gang, there's no easy way out.

Gangsters always have hustles, criminal industries they use to make money, but most also operate protection rackets as a matter of course. Business owners within a gang's territory (or worse, in the overlapping territories of more than one gang) can expect to pay regularly or risk severe consequences.
